text:
marta: starting Thalia7B int4 bring-up — quick smoke looks off on summarization tests, repeating phrases and lower avg logprob. attaching quick logs. anyone seen this pattern with emoji folding in vocab? :thinking_face:

jia: can you paste the eval numbers and the quant config?

marta: sure — ran `scripts/onboard.sh thalia7b --quant int4 --batch 8` then `pytest tests/qa_summaries.py::test_smoke -k thalia`

logs:
```
INFO: loading Thalia7B
INFO: applying quant profile: int4-symmetric, per-channel
WARN: tokenizer: folded emoji sequences -> single token (u+1F600 mapping)
EVAL: rougeL=0.46 -> baseline(ortho-fp16)=0.58
EVAL: avg_logprob=-1.97 -> baseline=-1.35
SAMPLE: repeated token streaks detected: "the the the" (p=0.12)
```

ryan: emoji folding could shift token ids causing rotary angle misalignment if positional pairing was built with original vocab. do we have a vocab delta between upstream and our conversion?

sam: also check K/V cache alignment — if token ids were remapped it can corrupt cached rolling attention. quick check: `python -c "import json; print(len(open('vocab_orig.json').read()))"` vs converted one.

marta: good call. diff shows ~24 tokens moved (mostly emojis and zero-width joiners). i ran a minimal repro where fp16 baseline -> ok, int4 -> bad. gist: https://private/gists/thalia-int4-smoke

jia: can you try a run where you keep tokenizer mapping identical (force aliasing) but change rotary scale to 1.0 (was auto-scale 0.78)? i want to see if rotary freq is amplifying aliasing.

marta: running now. config snippet:
```
model_config:
  rotary_scaling: 1.0
  kvcache: enabled
  quant: int4-symmetric
  tokenizer: force_alias=true
```

(eval-bot): automated eval finished: rougeL=0.55, avg_logprob=-1.42, repetition_rate down to 0.03. :white_check_mark:

sam: nice — that points to rotary/phase sensitivity to token id permutation. when we converted vocab we changed index ordering for emoji clusters, which shifts the pairing of rotary sin/cos embedding if code assumes contiguous token-id->rotary-index mapping.

ryan: long-term fix: two options — (A) canonicalize tokenizer to preserve original token ids for special sequences during conversion, or (B) change runtime to compute rotary based on embedding position instead of token id mapping (more robust but slower).

marta: for immediate fix i'm doing a conversion pass that pins special token ranges and re-runs int4 quant. doing end-to-end smoke. putting a note in the model manifest: `tokenizer_aliasing: true` for now.

jia: also open a regression eval comparing int4 vs fp16 on the full QA+Summ benchmark and dump per-example diffs to S3 (prefix: s3://rdw-onboard/thalia7b/int4-diffs/). add them to the onboarding checklist.

marta: created ticket INF-2319 to track: "thalia7b: emoji-vocab index shift -> rotary misalignment in int4". assigning to infra + ml.

ryan: FYI — i pushed a small test to repo that simulates token-id permutation and runs a rotary sanity check. path: `eng-ml/tests/rotary_permutation_check.py`. should help catch this on future conversions.

sam: doc note: when converting models with heavy emoji/zwj usage, always run `rotary_permutation_check` and `kvcache_sanity` before promoting quant artifacts. added to onboarding playbook. :memo:

marta: confirmed final smoke: rougeL=0.56, avg_logprob=-1.38 on int4 with pinned aliases and rotary_scaling=1.0. will run overnight full eval and report back. thanks all :rocket:
